**What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities: visual clarity from above, performance, vanilla parity.

**⚠⚠ THE FORTY-TWO RULES:** 1. CLAMP AT SELECTION. 2. NEVER PATCH `TryRebuildDirtyRegionsAndRooms`. 3. REGION CONNECTIVITY IS MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE PATHFINDER: flood CELLS. 4. COUNT EMITTERS/POPULATIONS/ENGINE STACKS. 5 (§48): A `Touch` TARGET IS USUALLY UNWALKABLE. 6 (§49): A VANILLA HELPER CAN BE A NO-OP INSTEAD OF AN ERROR. 7 (§52): THE CARVE IS NOT THE LAST WORD. 8 (§52.6): A LOAD-TIME REPAIR PASS MUST NEVER RE-CREATE WHAT THE PLAYER DELIBERATELY REMOVED. 9 (§53): SOME MISPLACEMENTS ARE NOT VISIBLE IN THE CELL. 10 (§54): A STRUCTURE IS NOT A CELL. 11 (§55): A CELL-LEVEL VERDICT CANNOT AUTHORIZE A PAWN-LEVEL ACTION. 12 (§56a): A FOREIGN MOD'S MAP-SIZE SNAPSHOT IS AN INPUT YOU CAN CORRECT. 13 (§56g): NEVER COPY A GRID YOU DID NOT WATCH BEING WRITTEN. 14 (§56m): BEFORE RELOCATING DATA, ASK WHAT IS ALREADY AT THE DESTINATION. 15 (§57i): ASSERT ALWAYS, NARRATE ON REQUEST. 16 (§56o): COUNT THE FOREIGN MOD'S WRITE PATHS. 17 (§56q): A PASSING RUN THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE FAILURE IS NOT A FIX. 18 (§57a): NEVER EXONERATE A SUSPECT ON ONE CLEAN SAMPLE. 19 (§57f): `TicksGame` RESTARTS AT 0 EVERY NEW GAME. 20 (§57g): MOVING WORK EARLIER TURNS ON EVERY "IS THIS MAP READY" GATE. 21 (§58): THE PARALLEL GRIDS DO NOT TRAVEL WITH THE CONTENT. 22 (§59): A DERIVED GRID HAS NO PAWN IN IT. 23 (§60): AUDIT THE WEIGHTING, NOT THE SYMBOL. 24 (§61a): CLAMPING A VALUE WITHOUT CLAMPING ITS TARGET BUILDS AN OSCILLATOR. 25 (§61b): A POSTFIX ON `Update` IS AFTER THE OBJECT WAS ALREADY POSITIONED. 26 (§61f): EVERY READ OF THE MAP THE PLAYER CAN REACH MUST PASS THE RENDERER'S "IS IT DRAWN" GATE. 27 (§62c): PREFER SPAWN/DESPAWN OVER FLICK. 28 (§63a): A PERMANENT FICTION INSTALLED FOR ONE SUBSYSTEM IS READ AS FACT BY EVERY OTHER ONE. 29 (§0b): REPORT OUTCOMES, NOT INTENTIONS. 30 (§66d): A FELT DURATION IS A CHAIN, NOT A NUMBER. 31 (§66f): MAKE THE GUARD SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECLINED. 32 (§69a): TURNING OFF A TICK TURNS OFF EVERY SERVICE THAT RODE ON IT. 33 (§62k): A FILTER THAT CAN REJECT EVERYTHING MUST SAY SO. 34 (§62l): AN INVISIBLE THING IS ABSENT FROM EVERY SECTION LAYER; MESH AND OVERLAYS ARE SEPARATE METHODS. 35 (§62n): A CLONED FOREIGN DEF MADE VISIBLE IS IN NONE OF THE HOST'S OWN LOOKUPS. 36 (§70a): RUN VANILLA'S OWN LEGALITY PREDICATE. 37 (§71a): NAME THE ENFORCEMENT POINT BEFORE NAMING THE SYMPTOM. 38 (§73): WHEN A SPRITE MUST APPEAR AWAY FROM ITS THING'S POSITION, OWN THE DRAW. 39 (§76): WINNING THE LAST WRITE DOES NOT SETTLE A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT THE TARGET - SUSPEND THE OTHER DRIVER INSTEAD. 40 (§75.h): A TRIPWIRE THAT FIRES BEFORE THE OBSERVER ATTACHES IS NOT A TRIPWIRE - GIVE EVERY STARTUP ASSERTION AN IN-GAME READBACK. 41 (§77a): A STRUCT FIELD YOU NEVER SET IS A FEATURE YOU NEVER SHIPPED - `PawnDrawParms.facing` sat writable in a postfix we already owned for two windows while pawns walked backwards down the stairs. 42 (§77b): THE DIRECTION A MOTION READS AS IS A PROPERTY OF THE THING, NOT OF THE ARRIVAL - and the far end is a DIFFERENT thing with its own axis, so the arrival half needs the FAR link's geometry, never the journey's.

# 74. BLUEPRINT FINISHED-ART LOOK — SHIPPED w10, USER-VERIFIED

ABBlueprintLook static-ctor retint, Blueprint_ABBuild stuff tint, ABGhostGraphicForLinks IsDoor bypass. The single knob is `ABBlueprintLook.BlueprintAlpha`, consumed in two places: the generated blueprint `GraphicData.color` and `Blueprint_ABBuild.DrawColor` (which must re-apply it on top of the stuff color, or a stuffed plan comes back fully opaque).

**§74.b (w11, post-ship field report):** shipped value 0.70 read as ALREADY BUILT in game - dark-wood link art over dark stone has enough contrast at 70% to pass for a finished building, and unlike vanilla we removed the blue `BlueprintColor` wash that used to do the "this is a plan" signalling on its own. Dropped to **0.42**, i.e. below vanilla's own 0.6 blueprint alpha, since our art is full-color where vanilla's is a desaturated wash and therefore needs more transparency to read as equally provisional. ⚠ NOT yet field-confirmed at the new value; if it now reads too faint the fix is that one constant, and the honest next step is a small tint (cool wash at low strength) rather than chasing alpha further, because alpha alone trades "looks built" against "can't see it".

# 75. WALL RISERS — SHIPPED w10 (a-h), USER-VERIFIED, PLACEHOLDER ART

4 defs; a riser IS a `Building_ABColumn`; WallLamp attachment mechanics; no `holdsRoof`; cascade despawn with its wall; north-face uiIconPaths. **f:** no `researchPrerequisites` on `AB_ColumnBase`/`AB_WallRiserBase` (⚠ per-network toggles still respect each host's research via `AB2_ColumnNeedsResearch`); architect uiOrder links 2060-2066, columns 2070-2073, risers 2080-2083 (they had been inheriting DoorBase's 2010).

**§75.g PROBE:** `AB2: carrier probe` (`DebugActionType.ToolMap`). Click a cell: every thing with def/class/drawerType/`IsCarrier`/`ShouldPrint`, an explicit DYNAMIC DRAW flag when a carrier is not `MapMeshOnly`, the foreign print-binding census, and a live **patch census** from `Harmony.GetAllPatchedMethods()` + `GetPatchInfo(m).Prefixes[].owner`. Built because four static facts contradicted the symptom and only the game could say which was false. **Keep this tool.**

**§75.h THE REAL FIX.** §75.d aimed at `SectionLayer.TakePrintFrom`; the probe's census showed only vanilla's general layer patched and NOT ONE Dubs layer. Decompiling: `Rimefeller.SectionLayer_ThingsPipe` and `DubsBadHygiene.SectionLayer_ThingsSewagePipe` (identical shared Dubwise code) derive from plain `SectionLayer`, declare NO `TakePrintFrom`, and override `Regenerate()` to walk cells calling **`Building_Pipe.PrintForGrid(SectionLayer)`**. `DeclaredMethod(layer,"TakePrintFrom")` was always null → silent `continue` for two windows. ⚠ The rule-33 tripwire HAD been firing correctly the whole time, into Player.log only, because it runs before the bridge attaches (rule 40).

Now: patch `<Host>.Building_Pipe.PrintForGrid` per host (DBH / Rimefeller / Rimatomics), deduped by MethodInfo. ⚠ The prefix INSPECTS the `SectionLayer` argument, because one method serves the normal-view layer AND the host's `*Overlay` layers: it refuses only for layer types in the resolved `NormalViewLayers` set, so anything unrecognised prints and a future rename leaks art rather than hiding connectivity (rule 34, fail-safe direction). `__instance` typed `Thing`, layer bound by index, no foreign type in any signature. A `Census` string records per-host binding, read back by `AB2: network scan` and the probe.

# 76. PERSPECTIVE SHIFT — SHIPPED w10, USER-VERIFIED

Suspend `Avatar.UpdateCamera` via a parameterless prefix while the viewed band is not the avatar's, rather than out-writing PS (rule 39: our clamp already ran last and that was exactly the problem - the camera settled at our own loose lower bound, `minZ - half*0.5f`, which is the gutter). On transit, snap the camera and NULL `Avatar.physicsPosition`, which outranks `pawn.Position` in PS's target expression and would otherwise drag the view back to the level just left. Freeze via `State.CameraLockPosition` (`ControlsFrozen` is read-only computed); setting `psFreezeAvatarWhilePeeking`, default true, checkbox rendered only when `PerspectiveShiftCompat.Present`; `lockedByUs` guards release so we never clear a lock PS itself set. Cross-band SHOOTING and stair TRAVERSAL needed no code at all: PS gates on `verb.CanHitTarget`, which funnels through our existing `TryFindShootLineFromTo` patch.

# 77. TRANSIT ANIMATION REWORK — MOCKUP ROUND 2, OPEN

**Trigger (w11 field report):** the §73 clips "do not feel interactive or part of base game", worst under Perspective Shift; pawns do not face the right way on stairs. Reference points named by the user: Melee Animations, Flourish. NOTHING IN `Source/` HAS BEEN TOUCHED - this section records the study only.

**⚠ §77a THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST (rule 41).** `PawnDrawParms.facing` is a plain writable `Rot4` field on the struct our `Patch_PawnRenderer_ABBelowShrink` postfix already receives by ref. The §73 banner's "NO ALPHA / scale is the only channel" was true and is still true, but it quietly implied the pose had only one channel. It has two. Nobody ever sets facing, so a pawn walking north into a stairwell keeps whatever the pather left - most often south, i.e. **walking backwards down the stairs**. `ShouldRecache` already compares facing, and `IsAnimating` already vetoes the cached atlas blit for the whole clip, so the fix is ONE line next to the existing `pose.hide` branch plus an `int facing` on `ClipPose`. **Takeable on its own, independent of which language wins.**

**⚠ ALPHA, RE-CHECKED AND STILL NO.** `parms.tint` is writable too and `PawnRenderNodeWorker` does `matPropBlock.SetColor(Color, parms.tint * material.color)` - but a pawn's material is cutout, so alpha only lands if `PawnRenderFlags.Invisible` is also set, which routes every node through `InvisibilityMatPool.GetInvisibleMat`: a distinct shader with a noise distortion texture and a hard-coded cyan `(0.75, 0.93, 0.98, 0.5)` multiply. That is a cloak effect, not a fade. **The scale-only grammar stands.** `Vanish()` keeps its job and the mockups add its mirror, `Reveal()`.

**§77b THE RAILING BUG - IT IS AT BOTH ENDS, AND THE SHIPPED CODE HAS BOTH.** Two user field reports on the mockups, one per end. Settled by decoding the PNGs (alpha bbox + per-edge opaque coverage in a 6px band), not by eye.

*The art convention, measured.* Every `*_south` sprite has its notch - the gap in the black frame - on its **NORTH** edge (`AB_StairsDown_south` north-edge coverage 42% against 88/99/87), with the tread shading running light->dark toward the south. Same for the grand staircase and the ladder. The rotation names the direction the stairs **lead**; the way in is the opposite edge. So **entry edge = `Opposite(Rotation)`, run direction = `Rotation.FacingCell`.**

*Near end.* `ABStairAnim.NotifyTransited` computes `IntVec3 approach = near.Position - prePos` - **the direction the pawn arrived from**. On three approaches out of four that walks the clip straight through a handrail. The fallback branch below already uses `near.Rotation.FacingCell`; that is what the MAIN path should use.

*Far end - and this one is subtler.* ⚠ **The counterpart is spawned with the SAME `Rotation`, and that is a load-bearing invariant, not an oversight** - `GenAdj.AdjustForRotation` shifts an even-sized footprint by a cell (the 2x2 stairs and elevator are even on both axes) and `TryCellPairs` pairs cell i to cell i; the banner in `Building_ABStairs2` documents the "stairs work sometimes" bug that came from getting it wrong. **Do not flip it.** Same rotation means the counterpart's notch is on the SAME side, so a pawn that rose through the shaft surfaces at the **deep end** of the far run (correct - that hole is the top of the flight it just climbed) and must walk out along **`-far.Rotation.FacingCell`**, i.e. the reverse of the direction it walked in on the level below. Therefore:
- `entry pose  forward = near.Rotation.FacingCell`
- `emerge pose forward = -far.Rotation.FacingCell`   ← a different vector, from a different building
- `LandingCell` (ABWormholePather) must prefer the far link's **entry-side** cell, `far.Position - far.Rotation.FacingCell * (size/2 + 1)`. It currently prefers the anchor's own cell and then a random cell within `LandingRadius`, so the pawn routinely lands outside the railing.

*Near-side pathing.* Nothing restricts which side a link is entered from: `PlaceWorker_ABLinkApproach` accepts ANY cardinal neighbour of ANY footprint cell (deliberately generous, for good reasons in its banner) and `TrySegment` rewrites the destination to `near.Position` with no side preference. A real fix makes the transit anchor the entry cell, `near.Position - near.Rotation.FacingCell * (size/2 + 1)`, **with a fallback to today's behaviour when that cell is blocked or unreachable** - a link must never become unusable, that is the ladder-to-nowhere class of bug.

*The art is not centred in its own footprint.* Measured centre offsets, cells: `StairsDown` N(0,-0.20) E(-0.11,+0.42) S(0,+0.22) W(+0.11,+0.42); `StairsUp` N(0,-0.31) S(0,-0.11); `GrandStairsDown` N(0,-0.21) S(0,+0.23); `GrandStairsUp` N(+0.02,-0.37) S(+0.02,-0.02); ladder ~0; elevator 0. Walking to the CELL centre walks off the drawn treads. Ports as a constant added to the pose offsets, which are already in draw space.

**⚠ §77c ART DEFECTS, SAME MEASUREMENT PASS - USER'S DOMAIN, NOT TOUCHED.** (a) `AB_GrandStairsDown_east`/`_west` and `AB_GrandStairsUp_east`/`_west` are the NORTH composition unrotated (1.85 x 2.43 cells, a north-south run), so a grand staircase placed east or west shows treads across the direction of travel. (b) `AB_StairsDown_east`/`_west` are a different composition from the north/south pair (1.24 x 1.17 vs 0.83 x 1.47) and sit 0.42 cells north. (c) `AB_StairsUp_east`/`_west` span the full 2 cells with no notch resolving on any edge. (d) `AB_LadderUp_east` is a 0.14-cell sliver drawn 0.30 cells WEST of its own cell. The mockups print a per-rotation ART warning under the affected panel so this is never re-diagnosed as an animation fault.

**THE FIVE LANGUAGES** (`mockups/anim-A..E-*.html`, shared engine in `mockups/kit/`). Each page carries all four link types over the REAL `AB_*.png` art, a 4-facing schematic pawn, a scrubbable phase timeline with the stagger window hatched, a **Perspective Shift avatar view** with a controls-frozen badge, gold/red **footprint edge markers** (gold = the edge the art is open on, red = railing), and a **live C# port panel** that transliterates the running JS into `ClipPose` code. Machine-checked: all poses finite and in range, and **no pose on any page crosses a railing or leaves the run through a closed end**, over 4 rotations x 2 journey directions x 61 samples x both phases.

- **A - Doorway.** Never break the walk cycle; depth ramp starts at 35% instead of tick 1; mouth clips late and fast. 18/22/25/18t. Lowest risk, biggest latency cut.
- **B - Weight.** Anticipation-action-recovery on every beat, non-uniform `sx`/`sz`, crouch before commit, look-back beat on the grand staircase. Up to 54t of stagger - the Melee-Animations register, and the WORST option under PS.
- **C - Traveler.** Entry and emerge run in ONE window; origin ghost and landing draw are both live, matched in scale and position at p=0.5 so the band cut is seamless. The direct answer to the PS complaint. Only language that edits the clip LIFECYCLE (emergeStart=0, `hide` retired, `IsGhosting` needs its own flag, `FollowTransit` fires at entryTicks/2).
- **D - Machinery.** Pawn stays calm, the BUILDING acts: staircase dims with a travelling cast shadow, ladder flexes on the pull, elevator car dims/shrinks/thumps. Needs an owned draw (rule 38) - overlay copy preferred over `MapMeshAndRealTime` on all four defs. No new art: existing PNGs + Core's `SkyfallerShadowCircle`.
- **E - Beat.** 10-14t, one strong pose, **staggerTicks = 0** so the pawn is never taken off the player and the emerge accent plays over real movement (offsets capped at 1/4 of the anchor vector for that reason). Best under PS purely because nothing is ever frozen.

**⚠ C AND D ARE ORTHOGONAL** - C is a lifecycle change, D is a draw addition. The strongest combination available is C's window with D's rig track, and neither page assumes the other.

**⚠ UNVERIFIED IN THE MOCKUPS:** the sign of `o.rot`. The studies rotate in screen space; in game the pose becomes `Quaternion.Euler(0, rot, 0)` about the up axis and the handedness has not been checked against a running frame. If leans read mirrored, negate. Also: E's no-stagger emerge is drawn over a pawn that is genuinely walking, and the path line (`ABTransitVisuals`) is drawn at TRUE world coordinates, so large emerge offsets would visibly desync sprite from line.
